questions.q: What does cancelling an invoice do?
options: Only removes one distribution line
Automatically pays the invoice in full
Converts the invoice into a credit memo
Sets the invoice and installment amounts to zero, reverses all distributions, and reverses any PO matches
questions.explain: Cancelling is an all-or-nothing action at the invoice level, undoing the invoice's accounting and matching entirely.

options: Only unpaid invoices that are either unapproved, or approved with no effective payments or posting holds
Any invoice, regardless of payment status
Only invoices that have already been fully paid
Only credit memos
questions.explain: Cancellation is restricted to unpaid invoices meeting specific approval/hold conditions.

questions.q: What happens when you reverse a specific invoice distribution?
options: The entire invoice is deleted
A new offsetting distribution with a negative matching amount is created, and related PO information (like quantity billed) is updated if applicable
The supplier is automatically merged
The invoice number is automatically changed
questions.explain: Reversing a distribution is a granular operation that offsets just that one distribution, leaving the rest of the invoice intact.

questions.q: When should you cancel a whole invoice rather than reverse a distribution?
options: When only one distribution out of several needs correcting
Whenever the supplier is international
When the invoice itself shouldn't exist at all, such as a duplicate entry
Whenever the invoice amount is under $1,000
questions.explain: Cancelling suits invoices that shouldn't exist entirely; reversing a distribution suits correcting one piece of an otherwise legitimate invoice.

questions.q: What do cancelling and reversing have in common regarding paid invoices?
options: Both are generally restricted once a payment exists, consistent with the adjustment restrictions from the previous lesson
Both work freely on paid invoices with no restriction
Cancelling works on paid invoices but reversing does not
Reversing works on paid invoices but cancelling does not
questions.explain: Once an invoice has an actual payment against it, both operations run into the same payment-related restrictions as ordinary adjustment.
